3Summarize prior conversation history when full history is no longer needed.
4Validate the model's structured output against the expected schema.
5Move stable repeated content into a cacheable prefix at the head of the prompt.
6Trim retrieved passages to spans relevant to the user's question.

Options for each row: Output Handling / Prompt Construction / Input Preparation
questions.examAns:
1 → Output Handling
2 → Prompt Construction
3 → Input Preparation
4 → Output Handling
5 → Prompt Construction
6 → Input Preparation
questions.examAnsDesc:
Explanation: Quy tắc: xử lý NGUYÊN LIỆU trước khi lắp prompt (summarize history, trim passage) = Input Preparation. Bố trí bên trong prompt (thứ tự section, cacheable prefix) = Prompt Construction. Sau khi model trả về (validate, persist) = Output Handling.

Distractors: 'Cacheable prefix' và 'thứ tự section' dễ bị nhầm sang Input Preparation — nhưng cả hai là QUYẾT ĐỊNH BỐ CỤC PROMPT.

Tip: chuẩn bị nguyên liệu=Input; bố cục prompt=Construction; validate/lưu=Output

Theo lời giải trong bộ đề gốc (chưa đối chiếu lại với tài liệu của Anthropic).

questions.examQue: A customer support team has proposed delegating customer refund decisions to a Claudedriven workflow with no human review for refunds under 50 USD. The team's reasoning is that small refunds are low-risk and human review would erase the efficiency gain. Which Delegation-competency principle should guide your response?
questions.examAnsDesc:
Explanation: Delegation đúng = phân loại theo BẢN CHẤT rủi ro (khả năng hồi phục, rủi ro pháp lý/danh tiếng, tính hệ thống), không theo con số giao dịch.

Distractors: A và D cực đoan (bỏ hết hiệu quả), C cực đoan ngược lại. Đáp án đúng luôn là nguyên tắc ở giữa.

Tip: delegation scope theo LOẠI rủi ro, không theo số tiền

Theo lời giải trong bộ đề gốc (chưa đối chiếu lại với tài liệu của Anthropic).
options: Delegation should always include human review on every decision the workflow produces.
Delegation scope should reflect the type of risk involved, not the transaction size alone.
Delegation scope should be set primarily by maximizing efficiency gains across the workflow.
Delegation should be avoided entirely wherever financial transactions occur in the workflow.

questions.examQue: You are identifying inefficiency in a Claude Code workflow where each engineer manually re-explains the project's conventions and architecture in every session. Which adjustment most directly removes this inefficiency?
questions.examAnsDesc:
Explanation: Persistent project context (CLAUDE.md) commit vào repo = viết một lần, mọi session của mọi người đều tự nạp.

Distractors: Các phương án khác là joke-distractor — dấu hiệu câu dễ, không nên mất thời gian cân nhắc.

Tip: lặp lại context → CLAUDE.md trong repo

Theo lời giải trong bộ đề gốc (chưa đối chiếu lại với tài liệu của Anthropic).
options: Forbid the use of Claude Code on the project entirely to avoid the session-initialization overhead, accepting that the team loses all AI-assisted development productivity for this codebase.
Capture the project's conventions and architecture in a project-scoped CLAUDE.md (or equivalent persistent project-context file) committed to the repository, so each session loads it automatically.
Tell each engineer to retype the project conventions and architecture context more quickly at the start of each session, reducing time lost without eliminating the repeated manual effort.
Remove all documented project conventions and architectural standards so engineers have nothing to re- explain at session start, accepting the loss of consistency and shared coding standards.

questions.examQue: The compliance team has authored a regulatory disclosure procedure that must be applied identically across customer service, sales, and onboarding workflows. The procedure changes when regulators issue updates, currently four to six times per year. You are designing how the procedure will be packaged for use by Claude across all three workflows. Which two design decisions should you include? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
questions.examAnsDesc:
Explanation: Yêu cầu: áp dụng y hệt + đổi 4–6 lần/năm + một chủ sở hữu ⇒ một Skill duy nhất do compliance team sở hữu (A), được cả ba workflow tham chiếu (E). Sửa một chỗ, áp dụng mọi nơi.

Distractors: B tạo 3 bản copy (drift ngay lần cập nhật đầu). C biến procedure thành dữ liệu tra cứu, không bảo đảm áp dụng y hệt. D là drift có hệ thống.

Tip: identical procedure + đổi thường xuyên = 1 Skill, 3 nơi tham chiếu

Theo lời giải trong bộ đề gốc (chưa đối chiếu lại với tài liệu của Anthropic).
options: Package the procedure as a Claude Skill owned directly by the compliance team.
Embed the procedure text into each workflow's system prompt at integration time.
Store the procedure in a shared retrieval corpus accessed by all three workflows.
Have each workflow team rewrite the procedure for its own context.
Reference the same Claude Skill from all three workflow integrations.

questions.examQue: You are compiling continuity practices that span the deployment lifecycle. Which two practices belong on the list? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
questions.examAnsDesc:
Explanation: Continuity = TÀI SẢN ĐO LƯỜNG được mang đi (B: eval framework + reference set) + TRI THỨC được chuyển tiếp giữa các pha (D: lessons learned).

Distractors: E chống lại chính tinh thần iteration. A và C là lưu trữ/thông báo, không tạo tính liên tục thực chất.

Tip: carry forward eval framework + lessons learned

Theo lời giải trong bộ đề gốc (chưa đối chiếu lại với tài liệu của Anthropic).
options: Maintain a stakeholder register and notify the listed parties at every phase transition event.
Carry the evaluation framework and reference set forward across iterations rather than rebuilding each time.
Archive every phase deliverable in long-term storage to preserve a record of what was produced.
Capture lessons learned at the end of each phase and surface them as inputs to the next phase.
Lock decisions made in early phases to prevent revisiting them as later phases begin.

questions.examQue:
You are running a discovery engagement for a new Claude-based capability and must complete the requirements-gathering steps before validating with stakeholders.
Which two steps must be completed BEFORE validating the captured requirements with stakeholders? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
questions.examAnsDesc:
Requirements must first establish what the capability is expected to accomplish, who will use it, and which constraints bound the solution. Option B captures the business purpose, success criteria, and intended user population. Option E identifies critical non-functional requirements that will influence model selection, integration patterns, deployment boundaries, evaluation design, and operational controls. These inputs must exist before stakeholders can validate whether the captured requirements accurately represent their needs.

Architecture decision records are produced after meaningful alternatives and design decisions exist. Detailed traceability is important but follows the initial elicitation and consolidation process. Rollout scheduling occurs later, after requirements and architecture have been validated. Anthropic likewise recommends defining measurable success criteria and empirical evaluation methods before optimizing prompts or finalizing the implementation.

Tip: business goals & user population (B) + non-functional constraints (E) before validating with stakeholders
options: Produce architecture decision records that capture the rationale for major design choices.
Capture the business goals, success criteria, and the in-scope user population for the engagement.
Document the consolidated requirements with traceability to the source stakeholder for each item.
Schedule the rollout milestones and dependencies with engineering and product partners.
Identify the non-functional constraints covering latency, cost, audit, data sensitivity, and regulatory needs.

questions.examQue:
You are comparing two configurations for an internal compliance Q & A assistant. Configuration X reduces top-k retrieval and uses a lighter model, lowering p95 latency by 38 percent while producing a measured 2 percent reduction in the accuracy benchmark. Configuration Y retains the existing top-k retrieval setting and heavier model, with unchanged p95 latency and no measurable change in accuracy. The deployment's stated priorities are accuracy first and latency second.
Which configuration is the better recommendation?
options: Configuration X, because the 2 percent accuracy reduction falls within normal benchmark variance and is not a meaningful regression.
Configuration Y, because the deployment's stated priority is accuracy first, and Configuration X produces a measured reduction in accuracy.
Configuration X, because lower latency generally matters more than accuracy, regardless of the deployment's stated priorities.
Configuration X, because a 38 percent latency improvement outweighs a 2 percent accuracy reduction as a general rule across compliance deployments.
questions.examAnsDesc:
Configuration Y is the appropriate recommendation because architectural optimization must follow the deployment's explicitly defined priorities and acceptance criteria. Accuracy is the primary requirement for this compliance assistant, and Configuration X introduces a measured two-percent accuracy regression. That reduction cannot be dismissed as ordinary benchmark variation unless repeated evaluation establishes that it is statistically insignificant.

In a compliance workload, even a small accuracy decline can increase incorrect guidance, missed policy requirements, human-review effort, and regulatory exposure. Configuration Y preserves the established accuracy level while maintaining the current latency profile. Although its latency does not improve, latency is explicitly the secondary objective. Configuration X could be reconsidered only if further testing eliminates the accuracy regression or stakeholders formally approve a revised trade-off.

Tip: accuracy first priority -> reject 2% accuracy regression despite 38% latency gain (Configuration Y)

questions.examQue: You are defining where human review must remain in a planned automated pipeline. Which placement reflects sound human-in-the-loop design?
options: Place a human reviewer only after the irreversible action has already executed, making the review a post-hoc audit rather than a meaningful pre-action check or approval gate.
Place a human reviewer between the model's output and any high-impact, irreversible action, with explicit criteria for what the reviewer must check before approval.
Place a human reviewer in the loop for a randomly selected sample of requests, without defining criteria for what the reviewer should check or which output categories require mandatory review.
Remove all human review steps from the pipeline to maximize throughput, accepting that high-impact and irreversible actions will be taken without any human approval or oversight.
questions.examAnsDesc:
Sound human-in-the-loop design places review before a high-impact or irreversible action occurs. The reviewer must receive sufficient context and explicit approval criteria so that the checkpoint functions as a meaningful control rather than a ceremonial step. This is especially important when Claude outputs could initiate financial transactions, publish sensitive material, alter access rights, affect employment decisions, or trigger other consequential actions.

Option A provides only retrospective auditing and cannot prevent harm. Option C may support monitoring or quality measurement, but random sampling does not protect every case that requires mandatory approval, particularly when review criteria are undefined. Option D removes the accountability and intervention mechanism entirely. Therefore, B provides the strongest design by combining risk-based placement, human authority, and clearly defined verification requirements before execution.

Tip: HITL placement: between model output and high-impact/irreversible action with explicit check criteria (B)

questions.examQue:
You are selecting the documentation set that should accompany a Claude-based deployment at handoff.
Which set is most complete?
options: Architecture overview, ADRs, component-level diagrams, runbooks for common operations, an on-call playbook, and a list of known limitations.
Code comments scattered across individual source files with no integrating architecture overview, no ADRs, no runbooks, and no on-call playbook to orient operators or new team members.
A single one-page architecture diagram with no ADRs, no runbooks, no on-call playbook, and no list of known limitations to support operators or future maintainers.
A verbal handover walkthrough conducted on the day of transition, with no written architecture overview, ADRs, runbooks, playbook, or known limitations captured for future reference.
questions.examAnsDesc:
A complete handoff package must help different stakeholders understand, operate, troubleshoot, and evolve the Claude-based solution. An architecture overview explains the system's structure and responsibilities, while Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) document important decisions, alternatives, and trade-offs. Component-level diagrams provide implementation context without forcing maintainers to reconstruct dependencies from source code. Operational runbooks and an on-call playbook enable reliable incident detection, diagnosis, escalation, and recovery. Documenting known limitations is particularly important for Claude applications because model behavior can vary with prompts, context, input distribution, and external dependencies.

Options B, C, and D each provide only a partial or temporary understanding of the system. They would create knowledge gaps, increase operational risk, and make future maintenance dependent on individuals rather than durable organizational documentation.

Tip: Complete handoff doc set = Architecture overview + ADRs + component diagrams + runbooks + on-call playbook + known limitations (A)

questions.examQue:
A Claude architect is configuring a shared Claude Code environment for a twelve-person development team.
Which two configuration decisions most directly establish a consistent, secure team environment? (Select two.)
options: Commit shared MCP server definitions and tool permissions in project-scope configuration files alongside the repository.
Apply managed configuration to enforce non-overridable security and compliance policies across all team members.
Set editor theme and display preferences at the project scope so they are uniform across workstations.
Instruct each engineer to configure their preferred Claude model in personal user-scope settings.
Store the team's shared API key in the project-scope settings.json so all engineers use the same credential.
questions.examAnsDesc:
Project-scope configuration is appropriate for shared MCP definitions, permissions, hooks, and other repository-specific behavior that every team member should receive consistently. Managed configuration complements this by enforcing organization-wide security and compliance requirements that individual developers cannot override. Together, these mechanisms separate collaborative project configuration from centrally controlled policy.

Editor themes are personal preferences and do not materially establish a secure environment. Allowing each engineer to select an arbitrary model can undermine consistency when model choice affects behavior, cost, or approved-use requirements. Storing a shared API key in a committed project file is a serious credential-management failure. Claude Code documentation identifies .claude/settings.json as the shared project file and managed settings as the highest-precedence organizational policy layer.

Tip: team config = project-scope MCP/tools in repo (A) + central managed non-overridable policies (B)

questions.examQue:
An engineer inadvertently commits an API key to the repository by placing it in .claude/settings.json.
Which configuration design principle was violated?
options: Project-scope configuration should always override user-scope configuration.
Managed configuration must be applied before project-scope configuration is read.
Credentials must be resolved at runtime from a secret store and never stored in version-controlled files.
MCP server definitions must reside in environment variables to prevent scope conflicts.
questions.examAnsDesc:
A shared project settings file is intended to be committed so that team-level configuration can travel with the repository. Consequently, it must never contain API keys, access tokens, passwords, or comparable secrets.

Credentials should be injected at runtime through an approved secret-management mechanism, environment-specific credential provider, or delegated authentication flow. This separates distributable configuration from sensitive authentication material and supports rotation, revocation, auditing, and least privilege.

Options A and B concern configuration precedence rather than secret handling. Option D is incorrect because MCP server definitions may legitimately be stored in project configuration; only their sensitive credential values must remain outside version control. Because the key was exposed, the operational response should also include immediate revocation or rotation and investigation of repository history.

Tip: secrets principle = resolve at runtime from secret store, never store in VCS (C)

questions.examQue:
You are designing the prompt for a ticket-triage classifier with thirty well-defined categories and clear category descriptions in the prompt.
Which technique is most appropriate as the starting point?
options: A chain-of-thought prompt for a routing decision that does not require multi-step reasoning.
A zero-shot prompt that specifies the categories with their descriptions and the required output format.
A prompt that demands the model invent new categories when the supplied ones do not fit.
A prompt with no category descriptions, expecting the model to infer the category set.
questions.examAnsDesc:
A clearly defined closed-set classification task should begin with a concise zero-shot prompt containing the permitted categories, unambiguous category descriptions, and the required output structure. This provides a simple, inexpensive baseline that can be measured against a representative evaluation set.

Chain-of-thought prompting adds unnecessary latency and token usage when the routing decision does not require substantive multi-step reasoning. Permitting Claude to invent categories would violate the closed-set contract and complicate downstream automation. Omitting descriptions would increase ambiguity among potentially overlapping labels. If evaluation later reveals persistent confusion between particular categories, the architect can introduce targeted examples or refine the definitions. Prompt complexity should be added in response to measured failure patterns, not assumed to be necessary before establishing baseline performance.

Tip: closed-set classification starting point = concise zero-shot prompt with clear category descriptions and output format (B)

questions.examQue: You are an operations lead choosing actions when a Claude conversation has degraded in quality. Which recovery action should be tried first when conversation quality degrades?
options: Summarize the current state and continue with a focused follow-up prompt.
Replace the model with a different vendor's model immediately.
Escalate to a senior architect for a manual review of the conversation history.
Discard the entire conversation and rebuild the work from the original prompt.
questions.examAnsDesc:
Summarizing the state and narrowing the next request applies Anthropic prompting best practices directly. If quality remains poor after this step, the user can then start a new conversation using the summary as its initial context.

Replacing the model immediately or discarding the entire conversation loses useful progress, while escalating to a senior architect adds unnecessary overhead before basic prompt recovery tactics are attempted.

Tip: degraded conversation quality -> summarize current state and continue with focused follow-up (A)

questions.examQue: A knowledge worker is explaining context-window basics to a teammate. Which statement most accurately describes a context window?
options: The subset of the conversation that the model determines is most relevant to the current input, which can be smaller than the full conversation.
A bounded amount of text the model can consider at once, including the conversation history, attached documents, and the current input.
The complete conversation history retained across sessions, which the model can reference whenever it produces a response in any chat.
An adjustable setting that determines how much of the conversation history the model includes in each response, configurable per chat.
questions.examAnsDesc:
A context window is a bounded amount of text the model can consider at once (conversation history, attached documents, and current input). Understanding this helps preserve relevant context and reduces conflicts between current and obsolete instructions.

The context window does not automatically persist across independent sessions without external state storage, nor is it a dynamic subset selected autonomously by the model at inference time or a per-chat response-history slider.

Tip: context window = bounded amount of text the model can consider at once (history + documents + current input) (B)

questions.examQue: You are a marketing manager deciding what to include in custom instructions for a writing-focused Project. Which two items belong in the custom instructions? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
options: A representative sample of past writing that reflects the team's preferred style and structure.
The brand voice and tonal expectations the writing must follow.
The preferred writing style of the marketing manager who will review all final deliverables.
The prompt author's preferred response length for internal messages unrelated to external deliverables.
The standard structure and length expectations for typical deliverables.
questions.examAnsDesc:
Custom instructions in a Project are designed to define consistent behavioral rules and expectations across all chats in that Project. This includes defining the brand voice and tonal expectations (Option B) and the standard structure and length expectations for typical deliverables (Option E).

A representative sample of past writing (Option A) belongs in Project Knowledge / uploaded reference files rather than instructions directly. Personal manager preferences (Option C) or irrelevant personal message length preferences (Option D) should not dictate project-wide instructions.

Tip: Project custom instructions = brand voice & tone (B) + standard deliverable structure & length (E)

questions.examQue:
An architect at Trenova Systems, Inc. is reviewing two draft communication packages for the same architectural decision. Package 1 contains a threat model, residual-risk register, and control-mapping table. Package 2 contains a list of capabilities delivered and feature-level roadmap dependencies.
Which two audiences are correctly matched to these packages? (Select two.)
options: Package 1 → engineering implementation team
Package 2 → executive sponsor
Package 1 → security and compliance reviewer
Package 2 → product manager owning the roadmap
Package 2 → security and compliance reviewer
questions.examAnsDesc:
Package 1 is designed for security and compliance review because its threat model identifies relevant threats and attack paths, its residual-risk register documents the risks remaining after controls, and its control-mapping table connects safeguards to organizational or regulatory requirements. Package 2 is designed for the product manager because delivered capabilities and roadmap dependencies directly support prioritization, release planning, sequencing, and lifecycle ownership.

An engineering implementation team would ordinarily need component diagrams, interface contracts, configuration schemas, deployment instructions, and operational runbooks rather than primarily risk-governance artifacts. An executive sponsor generally needs a concise outcome, cost, risk, and decision summary instead of feature-level dependency details. Effective architecture communication must therefore adapt the content and level of detail to each audience's responsibilities and decision rights.

Tip: Package 1 (threat model, residual risk, controls) → security & compliance reviewer (C); Package 2 (capabilities, roadmap dependencies) → product manager (D)

questions.examQue: A developer reports that Claude Code blocks a command that they believe should be permitted. The organization uses managed, command-line, local, project, and user-level permission settings. What is the safest first troubleshooting step?
options: Retry the same command repeatedly until Claude Code allows it.
Disable permission controls across all scopes to eliminate the denial.
Inspect the active permission rules across managed, command-line, local, project, and user scopes to identify the specific denying rule.
Grant unrestricted Bash access to bypass the denial.
questions.examAnsDesc:
Cần kiểm tra các permission rule đang có hiệu lực trên toàn bộ scope (managed, command-line, local, project, user) để xác định rule nào đang từ chối hành động. Sau khi tìm ra rule cụ thể, mới đánh giá xem có nên điều chỉnh hay giữ nguyên. Không nên tắt toàn bộ cơ chế permission hoặc cấp quyền Bash không giới hạn chỉ để vượt qua lỗi.

Tip: blocked command troubleshooting = inspect active permission rules across all scopes to find denying rule (C)

Nguồn tham khảo: CertEmpire CCAR-P Practice Test, Q2.

questions.examQue: You are designing a workflow in which Claude recommends rerouting a shipment. Once rerouted, the shipment cannot be returned to its original route without significant cost. Where should the human review step be placed?
options: After the shipment has already been rerouted, as a post-action audit.
Between Claude's recommendation and the execution of the reroute, with explicit review criteria and approval required before execution.
Only on a random sample of shipments, without mandatory review for high-impact actions.
Remove human review to preserve workflow throughput.
questions.examAnsDesc:
Human review phải nằm giữa kết quả đề xuất của model và việc thực thi hành động có tác động lớn hoặc không thể đảo ngược (irreversible action). Reviewer cần có tiêu chí đánh giá rõ ràng để kiểm tra trước khi phê duyệt. Kiểm tra sau khi hành động đã chạy chỉ là hậu kiểm (post-hoc audit), không thể ngăn ngừa thiệt hại.

Tip: high-impact / irreversible action -> human review between recommendation and execution with explicit approval criteria (B)

Nguồn tham khảo: CertLibrary CCAR-P, Q14.

questions.examQue: You are reviewing a draft Architecture Decision Record (ADR). It describes the selected architecture and includes technical implementation details, but it omits the alternatives considered and the trade-offs accepted. What should you ask the author to do before the ADR is published?
options: Delete the ADR and rely on the engineering team's collective memory.
Ask the author to document the alternatives considered and the trade-offs accepted before publishing.
Approve the ADR as written because documenting the selected decision is sufficient.
Replace the ADR with an unrelated architecture decision.
questions.examAnsDesc:
ADR cần ghi lại không chỉ quyết định kiến trúc được chọn mà còn phải bao gồm các phương án đã cân nhắc (alternatives considered) và các đánh đổi đã chấp nhận (trade-offs accepted). Những thông tin này giúp các kỹ sư và đánh giá viên sau này hiểu rõ cơ sở ra quyết định, tránh lặp lại các giải pháp đã bị bác bỏ và có thể đánh giá lại khi bối cảnh thay đổi.

Tip: ADR requirement = document alternatives considered and trade-offs accepted before publishing (B)

Nguồn tham khảo: DumpsTool CCAR-P Q&A, Q#9.
